claims.statement: `@komyuter/shared` is a private, source-only workspace package: its `exports` and `types` both point at `./src/index.ts`, it has no build/lint/test script, its only runtime dependency is `zod`, and its only consumers are `apps/server` (`workspace:*`) and `apps/admin` (`workspace:^`) — the Expo app `apps/mobile` does not depend on it.

`packages/shared/src/index.ts` is the package's only entry point and re-exports five type modules plus five schema modules with no subpath exports, so a name that is not re-exported from that barrel is unreachable to both apps.

`buildApp` creates Fastify with `withTypeProvider<ZodTypeProvider>()` and installs the zod `validatorCompiler` and `serializerCompiler` from `@fastify/type-provider-zod`, which is the wiring that turns shared zod schemas into server runtime behaviour.

Twelve admin CRUD endpoints attach shared create/update schemas as `{ schema: { body: … } }` across six resources (routes, directions, stops, detours, restrictions, fare configs); the login body is the only body schema defined outside the shared package.

A request body that fails a shared schema is rejected before the handler runs: `buildApp`'s central error handler maps a validation error to `422 { success: false, error: { code: "VALIDATION_ERROR", message } }`, maps `ApiError` to its own status/code pair, and falls back to `500 INTERNAL` with a logged error; `ApiError.code` is typed as the shared `ErrorCode` union.

No server route declares a `response` schema, so although the zod serializer compiler is installed, shared schemas constrain requests only and every success body is written literally as `{ success: true, data: … }`.

The geometry contract is structural only: `types/geometry.ts` defines `CoordinatePair = [number, number]`, `GeoPoint` (`type: "Point"` + one pair) and `GeoLineString` (`type: "LineString"` + pairs), and `schemas/geometry.ts` mirrors it with `z.tuple([z.number(), z.number()])`, GeoJSON type literals and a `.min(2)` coordinate-count rule for `LineString` — with no range check and no coordinate-order check.

Coordinate order `[lng, lat]` is a repository-wide convention settled by ADR-0013 (no conversion layer is to be added) that the two-number tuple cannot express; inside the shared package the only written statement of the order is the `SnapCoordinates` doc comment, and the order is otherwise carried by downstream consumers such as the write path's `ST_GeomFromGeoJSON` casts and MapLibre's native consumption.

`apps/server/src/domain/geometry.ts` layers a geographic range guard (`validateGeoPoint` / `validateGeoLineString`) on top of the shared geometry schemas, adding finite `lng ∈ [-180, 180]` / `lat ∈ [-90, 90]` checks and naming the coordinate order in its message, but no shipped request path calls those functions — their only importer is the unit test, so on the live API the enforceable geometry rules are the shared ones plus the write-path cast.

Enum string lists are duplicated between the type modules and the schemas: `types/domain.ts` declares `STOP_TYPE_VALUES` / `RESTRICTION_REASON_VALUES` / `RESTRICTION_AFFECTS_VALUES` as `as const` arrays while `schemas/domain.ts` spells the same literals out again in `z.enum([...])`, so adding a value requires editing two files the compiler does not correlate; `errorCodeSchema = z.enum(ERROR_CODES)` is the counter-example that derives from the const array instead.

Every resource in `schemas/domain.ts` follows a strict `createXSchema` plus `updateXSchema = createXSchema.partial().extend({ is_active })` pattern (routes already accept `is_active` at create), with schema-level rules that include the lower-case route-id slug regex, a hex-or-null `color`, `stop_order` as `int().min(1)` when supplied, restriction coordinate indices as `int().min(0)` with no `from <= to` ordering check, and absence of `stop_order` entirely on detour stops whose order is the array position.

The fare-configuration schema validates stored fare *parameters* only (`base_fare`, `base_distance_km`, `rate_per_km` nonnegative; student/senior discounts clamped to `[0, 100]`), and the package exports no fare computation of any kind; the two fare notions and the non-additive LTFRB formula are ADR-0001's, and the multi-criteria preference-profile weights remain tracked as planned/not implemented in `docs/DEVIATIONS.md` D9.

The wire envelope is declared twice but enforced nowhere: `types/envelope.ts` owns `ERROR_CODES` (six codes), `ErrorCode`, `ErrorBody` and `Envelope<T>`, and `schemas/envelope.ts` mirrors it with `errorCodeSchema` / `errorBodySchema` / success, failure and union envelope factories — yet in `apps/` only `ErrorCode` is imported (by `apps/server/src/api/errors.ts`); the server writes the success object literally and the admin unwraps it in its axios interceptor, which also rejects with client-synthesised codes (`NETWORK`, `UNAUTHORIZED`) that are not members of the shared union.

`types/export-dataset.ts` is the single source of the export document's identity: `EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION = "1.1"` and `EXPORT_COORDINATE_ORDER = "lng_lat"` are used as `typeof` literal types in `ExportDataset`, the assembler imports and stamps the same two constants, and the zod schema pins them as `z.literal(...)` — so bumping the version is one change that moves the produced document and its validator together.

The export contract's zod mirror (`schemas/export-dataset.ts`, including a `additional_distance_meters: int().nullable()` rule looser than the write-path `.min(0)`) is imported by nothing: `GET /api/admin/export/dataset` streams whatever `assembleExportDataset` returned, while the enforced contract is a second artifact — `specs/001-local-supabase-backend/contracts/export-dataset.schema.json` with `additionalProperties: false` at every level, compiled by Ajv in `apps/server/tests/helpers/dataset-schema.ts` — and the referential `referenceCheck` pass is exercised only by tests.

The Mapbox snap contract splits into an unapplied wire schema and a used-but-divergent type: `schemas/mapbox.ts` declares snake_case `distance_meters` (never attached to the route or applied by the client), while `types/mapbox.ts` documents `SnappedPath` as the camelCase counterpart with `distanceMeters`; the admin's `snapPreview` types the response as `SnappedPath` with no mapping layer, so `usePlottingStore` records an `undefined` `snap.distanceMeters` even though the server emits `distance_meters` — a latent disagreement with no current user-visible symptom, invisible to the store's tests because they inject camelCase fakes.

The overview read model is a type-only contract: `overviewRouteSchema` / `overviewStopSchema` exist so `apps/admin` can compile against the inferred `OverviewRouteEntity` (route cache, overview helpers, `listOverview`), while the server's `/api/admin/routes/overview` handler builds the payload from `loadDirectionFull`, declares no response schema, and therefore ships full stop entities where the declared shape says lean stops.

The full domain entity interfaces in `types/domain.ts` (`Route`, `Direction`, `Stop`, `Detour`, `DetourStop`, `Restriction`) are hand-written rather than inferred from the schemas, and only `FareConfiguration` has an importer (the admin fare API extends it); the server declares its own `*Entity` interfaces in `apps/server/src/domain/entities.ts` and the admin declares per-feature row interfaces, so the entity interfaces are documentation rather than a shared type every consumer uses.

The package has no test script of its own; the behavioural tests that pin its schemas live in the server suite (`apps/server/tests/unit/schemas.test.ts` and `tests/unit/geometry.test.ts`), and CI runs format check, lint, root typecheck, the admin suite and build — so a shared-schema regression reaches CI only through typecheck, with the behavioural tests left as a local pre-merge obligation.

Detour stops are the current shared contract model (`detourStopSchema`, `DetourStop`, `ExportDetourStop`) backed by the `detour_stops` table created in migration `0005` after migration `0004` dropped the `detours.notable_stops` JSONB column — so the `notable_stops` model and the `notableStopSchema` still described by `docs/DEVIATIONS.md` D7, ADR-0012 and `docs/ADMIN.md` no longer exist in this package.
